title: An agent answers a message by its id: `spawn ack <id> done|declined <why>` from its own pane, with no database login, recorded once; a task's report answers its delivery; the commands API and the agent page say each message acted, done or declined
prompt:
Read rsi/backlog/045.json and what landed for it (the message marker `[spawn message #<command id>]`, `message.taken`, the commands API's `message`, web/src/messages.ts); crates/spawn-cli/src/runtime.rs (`bridge_config`: a worker's pane gets no database login, the supervisor's gets its own) and crates/spawn-host/src/tmux.rs (`command_of`: no `SPAWN_*` variable reaches a pane but those the launch sets: SPAWN_AGENT_ID, SPAWN_SESSION_ID, SPAWN_EXECUTION_ID); crates/spawn-cli/src/deliver.rs (`collect_reports`, `new_report`, `put_aside`, `mark_delivery`: how the dispatcher reads what a worker writes in its workspace, safely, through crates/spawn-host/src/agent_files.rs; `task.reported` and its report; `task.delivered` names the command that delivered a task) and crates/spawn-cli/src/dispatch.rs (the pass that collects reports); crates/spawn-cli/src/main.rs (the commands; the usage lines and the contract scenario 010 that reads them); crates/spawn-core/src/event.rs (`EventKind`, `message.taken`); crates/spawn-postgres/src/fleet.rs (`SESSION_COMMANDS`); web/src/messages.ts and web/src/components/fleet/AgentDetail.tsx.

The problem. Objective 045 says when a message into an agent was typed, taken by its engine, and answered (the turn it started ended). Answered says the agent stopped, not that it did what the message asked, or that it chose not to: a person who asks a worker for something, or the supervisor who nudges one, cannot tell "done" from "ignored" without reading the transcript. A task has its report; any other message has nothing. GitHub #41 asks for an explicit answer by id.

Required behaviour.
(a) `spawn ack <command id> done|declined [<why>]`, run by an agent in its own pane: the answer to the message with that id. A why is required for `declined` (the words after the outcome, joined by spaces) and optional for `done`. It works in a worker's pane, which has no database login: no database variable is needed or read (the ack reaches the store through what the loop reads, as a report does, or another way that needs no login in the pane), and an ack made while the loop is down is recorded once it is back. It works from any directory in the pane (an engine's shell is often in a subdirectory of its workspace): it finds where the ack goes from what the pane was given at launch (for example a workspace variable the Bridge sets), never from the current directory alone, or it exits non-zero; it never says an ack was taken that the loop will not find. It exits 0 when the ack is taken for recording, and non-zero, saying why, for a missing or non-numeric id, an outcome other than done or declined, a decline with no why, or when run outside an agent's pane. The usage lists it (after the contract's line, which stays as it is).
(b) Recorded once: `message.acted {command_id, outcome, why}` in the agent's session, keyed by the message, within 10 s while the loop runs. The first ack of a message stands; a later one records nothing, whatever restarts. Whose ack it is, is decided by the loop from where it found the ack (that agent's workspace or its own record of the pane), never from a session or agent id the ack carries: an agent that sets SPAWN_SESSION_ID to another worker's session, or writes an ack file by hand, answers nothing of that worker's. An ack names a message into the session of the pane it is run in: one naming a message into another session, an unknown id, a command that types nothing, or a task's delivery (below) records nothing, and the loop's log says so.
(c) A task's report answers the message that delivered it (the command `task.delivered` names): Outcome `done` is `done`; `blocked` or `failed` is `declined`, with the Outcome line as the why. Recorded from the `task.reported` record, never twice.
(d) The commands API: the `message` of 045 gains `acted` (`{outcome, why}`, null until answered; `why` null for a done with none) and `acted_at_ms`; `state` is `acted` once answered, whatever else. The typed marker is followed by one line telling the agent how to answer (`spawn ack <id> done`, or `spawn ack <id> declined <why>`; for a task's delivery, that the report answers it), and 045's marker stays as it is.
(e) The page: `messageLine` appends " · done" or " · declined: <why>" after what 045 says (a why longer than 80 characters is cut to its first 79 and "…"). The agent page shows it.
(f) Nothing else changes: 045's lifecycle and alert, the report's rules, and the dispatcher's order stay as they are. docs/fleet-architecture.md says the ack, how it reaches the store, and that a report answers its delivery.

Out of scope: an alert or a Needs you item for a message never answered or declined; acks by the supervisor through its own login (it may use the same command); reading a reply's content.

Checked by rsi/scenarios/046.sh: a real `spawn loop` and `spawn serve` with four workers on a fake engine whose `spawn ack` runs in its own pane with every database variable unset: one acks (done; declined with a why; two refused forms; an ack of another worker's message, plain and with that worker's session named in SPAWN_SESSION_ID, a second ack and an ack of its own task's delivery that record nothing; an ack from a subdirectory of its workspace that is recorded; an ack made while the loop is down), one never acks (answered, never acted), one reports its task done and one blocked (their deliveries read done and declined); a restart changes no message; and messages.ts's words under node.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/, web/test/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/.
